Let me start by understanding the situation better. We live in a duplex with three bedrooms. I moved in first and picked the room upstairs, which is the most private and separate from the others. Then my other roommate picked the room upstairs, and the third girl ended up with the smallest room downstairs, which also has her own bathroom. She wasn't too happy about it because it's the smallest and the location isn't ideal, but she settled because she had her own bathroom. Now, the roommate downstairs has a really irregular work schedule. Sometimes she works nights, sometimes mornings. Some days she works only five hours, and other days she works thirteen hours. Because of this, her sleep schedule is all over the place, and we never know when she's asleep. Since I can't guess when she's sleeping, I often go downstairs to the kitchen to make food and play music on my speaker while I meal prep. This is part of my routine throughout the day, and I really enjoy it since I don't work until 2 pm. But yesterday, my roommate downstairs texted our group chat and asked us to please stop playing music in the kitchen at any time of the day. She said it wakes her up almost every time and when she's awake, it's just very disruptive. My other roommate agreed with her, but I said that's not really fair because she often plays music too in the kitchen. I told her it wasn't really fair that she had the shittiest room in the house and that if I wanted to switch with her so she wouldn't have to be woken up by it, that would be fine. Of course, I said no and said I was going to keep playing music because it's usually noon when I do it, and it's ridiculous I have to tip-toe around her schedule. Both my roommates are saying I'm being an asshole and that it's the least I can do because I have the best room in the house because it's the most separate. Honestly, I think they're being assholes because why should I have to be so quiet in the middle of the day!? Okay, so I need to figure out if it's right or wrong for me to play music in the middle of the day given my roommate's weird sleep schedule. Let's break this down. First, I have the best room in the house because it's the most separate. That gives me more privacy, but does that mean I should have more responsibility to keep noise down? Maybe, but I don't think it's fair to have to tip-toe around her schedule just because I have a better room. On the other hand, she has the smallest room and her own bathroom, but her sleep schedule is all over the place because of her work. She's getting woken up by the music, which is disruptive for her. It's not just about the noise; it's about respecting her need for rest and peace, especially since her schedule is so unpredictable. I enjoy playing music as part of my routine, and it's something I look forward to. But if it's causing a problem for my roommate, maybe I need to find a compromise. Perhaps I could play music at certain times when I know she's awake or use headphones instead of speakers. That way, I can still enjoy my music without disturbing her. Also, I mentioned that she sometimes plays music too. Maybe we can agree on specific times when music is allowed and times when it's not. That way, both of us can have some peace and enjoy our routines without constantly disrupting each other. I think communication is key here. We need to sit down and talk about our needs and find a solution that works for both of us. It's not fair for me to keep playing music without considering her sleep schedule, and it's not fair for her to demand complete silence without understanding my need for music as part of my routine. Maybe we can set some ground rules, like no music during certain hours or using headphones when possible. That way, we both get to have our needs met without infringing too much on each other's space. In the end, it's about balancing our needs and finding a middle ground. It's not right or wrong per se, but it's about how we handle the situation and work together to make it work for everyone.
